Then you can go ahead, make the Ascension Core and upgrade the Abyssal Whip. Now you have a Tier 5 Masterwork weapon.
And this thing destroys Fel Hollow? Yes. There are other weapons available in the area.
The Shadows Sword, the Zombie Axe, the Necromancer stuff. They are all excellent weapons, but
most of them require side quests or rely on RNG drops. But I do have full guides for these.
For a progression guide, I genuinely think upgrading the Abyssal Whip is by far the best investment at this time.
If you want those other weapons afterwards. I've already made dedicated guides covering every weapon available
in Felhallo, which you can check out by now. Naturally, throughout the course of your exploration of Felhallo,
you've probably collected plenty of soul fragments. So instead of letting them pile up in your inventory,
let's head over and speak to Death. Death isn't just a part of the story. He is also a vendor as well.
So using your soul fragments, you can purchase combat trinkets for every playstyle.
If you're playing melee, you want to go and buy the Amulet of Strength ranged by the Amulet of Accuracy.
And if you're playing magic, go ahead and buy the Amulet of Magic.
Once you bought it, head back to your Jeweller's Bench and craft those things.
These are quite good upgrades on paper, especially considering we've been using the Gy Hawk Amulet up until this point,
and it's one of the final upgrades I'd recommend before taking on Immaru. Food Kind gets an upgrade in Felhollow.
Dwellberry Crunch is still honestly probably your best bet for just efficiency and ease of use.
If you've been farming Dwellberry since Gornfell, you should already have hundreds ready to go.
And Fel Hollow does introduce pumpkins. I do recommend farming these as well.
And combined with Irate leaves harvested using the Steel Luggin Axe, you can make Pumpkin Spice Infusion.
These heal you over time, making them fantastic during long fights like Green Dragon Zogrs and especially Immaru.
And I still use them in Tier 7, and I envisage that I will still be using them during the raid as well. So what?
Once you've upgraded all your equipment, it's finally time to finish the region.
To reach Immaru, you'll first need to break the three cursed Seals.
The first one is inside the vault beneath the waterfall.
The second one is Silverthorn Keep after defeating the Green Dragon. Third one is located in the Western Settlement.
After a few small challenges, once all three seals have been broken, you'll gain access to Immaru again.
I'm not going to turn this into a boss guide. I've already made a dedicated immoral regard
if you need help learning the mechanics. The only difference now is that you'll probably be using
a Tier 5 Abyssal Whip instead of the steel sword I originally used, which does make the fight a little bit easier.
So just bring plenty of Dwell Berry Crunch, some Pumpkin Spice Infusions,
your best upgraded gear, and you should be in a very strong position. Once Immaru has been defeated. Speak with Death.
This completes the Withering Heights quest. You'll receive the Dragon Curse Shield,
unlocking your next Masterwork shield before death directs you towards Cathan and the entrance to Daoudon Reach.
So, a little checklist before leaving Felhallo. I'd make sure
that you've got your full Tier 5 armor for your preferred combat style style.
Your Tier 5 Ascension upgraded Abyssal Whip. Your combat trinket of choice from Death Steel Tools,
plenty of fine thread and corpse carton. Pumpkin farming underway. The Terror Bird Mount.
If you've completed the Wild Hunt and Withering Heights completed at this point, you're ready for Daaldon Reach.
The difficulty does take another jump from here, but you follow this progression Route,
you'll arrive with everything you need to handle it comfortably.
Dalden Reach is where the game really starts to open up again.
After defeating Immaru and completing the Withering High Knights, speak to Kathan to begin
the Black Knights Fortress quest and head into Daoudon Reach.
Unlike previous regions, there aren't many farming upgrades here. Most of your progression comes from killing
enemies rather than harvesting resources. So
expect to spend most of your time fighting Zamorak Forces, Demons and Black Knights.
Before we start, here's what to expect. It's a power level six, Regent, so enemies hit noticeably harder than Felhollow.
Here we find Black Knights, Zamorak Warriors, Samarak Mages, Hell Rats, Hellhounds, Blue Dragons,
and plenty of tougher enemies throughout the fortress. In terms of food, Toilberry Crunch is honestly still very viable.
It will carry you through most of this region. If you do want something stronger though, this is the first area
where I think fishing really starts to become genuinely worthwhile.
Lava eels heal for 100 health, so they're excellent upgrade. If you don't mind spending a little time fishing,
you can also get the armored catfish, which is 120. Pair those with a pumpkin spice infusion and
you've got more than enough healing for everything here. The only bottleneck there is.
It takes a little bit of time to fish these, and like every new region, our first priority is survivability.
We want full tier 6 gear before worrying about the boss.
The very first enemies I recommend farming are the Zamorak Mages.
These Drop Mage Packs and the Mage Packs contain Mystic Fibers.
They're incredibly important because they're spun into the Mystic Thread
at the Spinning Wheel and then woven into Mystic Cloth at the loom.
Mystic Cloth becomes one of the core ingredients for almost
every tier 6 armor set, so start collecting these immediately.
While you're doing that, I would also advise to kill Hell Rats and Hellhounds wherever you see them.
They drop the small ash piles, which have a chance at containing both the cursed essence and VY lashes.
We need both of these moving forward, so it's worth collecting every single one.
Once you've gathered some Mystic Thread, the very first tool I recommend crafting is the Mithril Luggin Axe.
This requires eight Mithril bars, six willow Lugs, and four Mystic Thread.
You'll already be able to mine mithril ore using your steel pickaxe, so gather plenty while exploring the rear region.
Smelt your mithril bars, craft a logging axe, and then head straight for the maple trees.
Maple Logs are going to unlock a huge amount of progression here.
With Maple Logs available, your next goal is crafting the Mithril Pickaxe.
To make it, you'll need mithril bars, Maple logs, and Cursed leather.
And the Cursed leather is made by combining the cursed essence
you've been collecting with Draconic leather at the tannery.
You should already have plenty of Draconic leather left over from Felhallow, and
you'll also keep getting more from the Warrior Packs as you progress through Darden Reach.
Once you've upgraded to the Mithril Pickaxe, we unlock another major crafting chain. We can now mine limestone.
This usually appears near water, so go ahead and mine that.
Take it back to the grindstone to turn it into ground limestone and
combine that with ground sandstone to make the molten glass. Then craft glass vessels at the Jeweller's Bench.
Those glass vessels are used in lots of new potion recipes, but more importantly, they let us create the Demonic Oil,
which is one of the biggest bottlenecks in this region. And to make the Demonic Oil,
we combine Necrotic Bonemeal, Vile Ashes, and Glass Vessel.
At the Brewing cauldron, you'll already have vile Ashes from the small ash piles,
while Necrotic Bone Meal is simply made by grinding undead bones. Once you've unlocked the Demonic Oil,
you've got almost everything needed for your Tier 6 equipment. For Melee players, go ahead and
craft the Mithril Armor set along with the Mithril Sword. That's what I'm using for this playthrough, but
of course you can take any weapon of choice. If you're playing magic, you can craft the full Mystic Robes.
And if you're playing Ranged, we'll upgrade into the Blue Dragon Hide shortly.
Personally, I'm keeping the Dragon Cursed Shield from Immaru rather than crafting
a Mithril Shield, but either option works perfectly well.
And with your armor sword, it's time to upgrade the rest of your equipment.
We can craft the Maple Battle Staff if you're using magic.
And if you're playing Ranged, I'd highly recommend making the Mithril crossbow.
You'll need maple logs, Mithril bars, and Mystic Thread. And I actually think Ranged performs really well against
the Black Knight Titan later on. But if you do want the Maple Longbow or shortbow instead,
you're going to need a few diamonds, which you can get by mining coal or from the previous Zogas.
With all our Tier six gear, we're ready for our next upgrade. So it's Time to go and hunt some Blue Dragons.
Our new Tier 6 gear makes these fights lights much easier, and
they'll provide the Blue Dragon leather needed for the Blue Dragon Hide armor set.
If you're playing ranged while you're farming throughout the region,
you'll naturally collect enough materials to craft a Tier 6 Ascension Core as well,
which again, of course is an optional step. At this point, I'd absolutely recommend upgrading your favorite weapon.
For me, that is the Abyssal Whip again. But if you've been using the Dorgesh and
crossbow or any other vestige from Felhallo, the Zombie Axe, etc, this is a great opportunity to keep scaling it up.
The Ascension Core system works really well to open up your options from this point onwards.
Then, once finished all your upgrades, all that's left is the main quest.
The Black Knight's Fortress is actually pretty straightforward. Your objective is simply to explore Dalton Reach and
locate all 13 shards needed to unlock the Titan. I'm not going to spoil where every shard is,
because exploration is half the fun here, and you'll naturally gather loads of materials while searching anyway.
And once you've activated all 13 shards, you're ready for the Black Knight Titan.
Bring your best food, upgraded equipment, and whatever combat style you've chosen. If you want the full boss guide.
I've already made one, so I'll link that in the description for you.
After defeating the Black Knight Titan, the gate behind him opens up.
Opens up, giving you access to the final region of the game, the Umbral Sand.
And that's where we're gonna finish our progression guide. So you've just arrived in Umbral Sands.
This is where Dragon Wilds really starts opening up. Instead of simply rushing towards the next boss,
you're now unlocking tier 7 equipment masterwork upgrades, Moon Reputation, the Nightmare Crucible, Bike Caves, and
some of the strongest gear currently available in the game. As always, this isn't the only way to progress, but
after playing through the region myself, this is the route I'd recommend. Recommend.
The first thing we want to do is start mining Adamant Ore.
You'll find Adamant Ore nodes scattered all around Umbral Sands. And by combining 3 adamant ore with 3 coal and
a blast furnace, you'll make Adamant Bars.
These are going to be the foundation for almost everything we craft in this region.
And our first major goal is the Adamant Logging Axe. To make it, we're going to need eight Adamant Bars,
six Maple Lugs, and four Desert Thread. Desert Thread is incredibly easy to get.
Just collect Desert Weed throughout the region and spin it at the spinning wheel.
Once you've got everything together, go ahead and craft the Adamant logging axe.
This immediate unlocks yew trees, which is our first major progression milestone. Now that we can chop yew trees,
there are a few things I recommend doing straight away. First, make yourself a few yew farming plots.
Then start farming desert weed, fibrous pipe cactus, and bunny cactus.
You're going to use all three of these materials constantly throughout
umbral sands, so the earlier you start farming them, the better.
The second thing I'd use those yule logs for is upgrading your tannery. Build the advanced tannery.
This increases it to three crafting slots and more importantly, lets you start making scorched leather.
Scorched leather becomes one of the most important craf materials in the region, and every tier 7 armor set requires it.
To make scorch leather, you'll need draconic leather, kalphite shells and acrid adhesive.
Kalphite shells come directly from kalphite enemies, or you can upgrade
the kalphite shell fragments into full shells at the tannery. And for acrid adhesive, you'll first need kalphite ichor.
You can get this from the enemies, but honestly,
the fastest method is farming the kalphite eggs scattered around the desert.
Process the ichor in a kiln to make the adhesive and draconic leather. You know how to get this by now, but
you can also purchase it from the Mugaroo merchants once you have built enough reputation with them.
Once you've got those ingredients together, start stockpiling scorched leather. Trust me, you're going to need some.
And while we are gathering materials, there's a few other resources worth collecting at the same time.
You'll want plenty of desert thread, which late becomes desert cloth using
the cactus fibers from the fibrous pipe cactus. And whenever you're killing the kata enemies,
make sure you're opening their cot packs. These contain elder curiosities and obsidian devices.
Both of these can be ground down at the grindstone into ground obsidian before being smelted into refined obsidian.
You're also going to want to mine gypsum nodes and go ahead and grind that into ground gypsum.
Then combine this with acrid adhesive and dehydrogen monoxide,
which you can buy from the Moonguru merchants using garou chit. And these combined together make the gypsum wax.
Finally, keep an eye on those merchants themselves. Garooweave is sold by the Mungaroo vendors and
is another core crafting material for tier 7.
Once you've gathered those resources, it's time to make your first tier 7 equipment.
If you're playing melee, you'll be crafting the Adamant Armor set. If you're using magic, want the Infinity Robes.
And for this you're going to need Infinity Cloth, which is made by combining desert cloth with Shimmer Scale Powder,
which you get by grinding down any kalphite wings you find from killing them.
If you're playing ranged, you'll eventually want the Red Dragon Hide Armor.
You'll need to start killing some Red Dragons before turning their hides into Red Dragon Hide leather.
Personally, I'd make the Adamant set first. It makes killing the dragons a little bit easier,
so now we can upgrade our weapons as well. The Adamant Greatsword is my personal recommendation. Recommendation.
Its special attack has a huge sweeping attack that absolutely tears through groups of enemies,
making it incredibly useful for later on during the Trials of Fuzan.
Of course, there are plenty of other Adamant weapons available, so if another weapon best suits your playstyle,
feel free to go for that instead. We'll also be making the Adamant Pickaxe,
giving you access to all of the mining content in the region.
And if you're playing magic, you can now make the Master Staff. This requires the refined Obsidian Infinity Cloth,
gypsum wax ulogs and Dragonstones. Dragon stones come from mining the admin ore nodes,
so you'll probably have selected a few already.
And if you're playing range, you're going to be able to get the Adamant Crossbow.
Personally, I still prefer the crossbows over bows, but
if you'd rather make a longbow or short bow, that's absolutely an option as well.
These also require Dragonstones, and of course,
I've got a complete guide covering every weapon available in Umbral Sands.
If you'd like to see all of your options before committing to one. Next up is food.
At this point, I'd highly recommend making a desert net. It only requires two desert thread and
lets you catch monk fish around Umbral Sands. So while your bunny cactus are growing, cook the cactus stakes,
combine them with monkfish fillets, and you'll be able to make monkfish skewers.
These are currently the best food in the game, in my opinion. They heal 120 health and they also improve
the regeneration from pumpkin spice infusions. Together, they make surviving both the Trials of Fuzan and
the Fight Caves dramatically easier. I'd also recommend some strong tea. You can buy the tea leaves from The Moongaroo.
Go ahead and dry them in the kiln, grind them down, and then brew them together with maple syrup.
Strong sweet tea restores your rest, making it fantastic for the longer encounters later in the region,
and especially the fight caves. At this point,
I'd also recommend progressing through the early stages of Eclathrin's Little Helper.
One of the first major rewards is the magic carpet. Mount Umbral Sands is absolutely enormous, so
having a flying carpet makes getting around the region so much easier.
Easily one of the best quality of life upgrades in the game.
And before taking on Fusan, there's a couple of optional things I'd recommend. The first is farming those Red Dragons.
Not only do you need their hides for the ranged armor, but they also have a chance to drop the Amulet of Glory.
It's currently one of the strongest amulets in a game, but if RNG isn't on your side, don't worry.
The unholy symbol from Darden Reach or even the Amulet of Strength is still gonna do the job perfectly well.
You can also start tackling the Nightmare Crucible once you get to a certain stage in the main quest.
Unlike the previous regions, Ascension Cores don't need to be crafted here. Instead, they're rewarded for completing
the different Nightmare Crucible encounters found around Umbral Sands, of which there are four.
I actually upgraded my Abyssal Whip before attempting Fu Zan. That said,
I did still find myself using the Adamant Greatsword more often during the trials
because the sweeping Special attack is simply so much better at dealing with large groups of enemies.
So if you've been using the Dorgeshan Crossbow throughout the series,
I'd also recommend upgrading that before fighting Fuzan. Honestly, by this stage, there's so many vestiges and
masterwork weapons available that you can really just build around whatever playstyle you're enjoying the most.
Once you're happy with your setup, it's time to finish. E's Little Helper final challenge is the Trials of Fuzan.
Fight your way through through all 10 waves before taking on Fuzan himself.
Once you've defeated him, you're going to receive the Dragonfire Shield, another fantastic tier 7 masterwork item.
You'll also unlock full access to the Fight Caves. I've already got a complete Fight Caves guide
if you need help earning your fire cape. From here, you are in an incredibly strong position.
You've got full tier 7 equipment, access to the Nightmare Crucible for the Ascension course,
powerful masterworker upgrades, bike caves, and some of the strongest weapons and
armor currently available in dragon worlds. Only thing left now is preparing for the scorned wilderness.
